draft.title: Isotopes
card: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons. They have the same number of protons, so the same atomic number, but different mass numbers.
Isotopes of an element react in nearly the same way, because they have the same number of electrons. For example, carbon-12 has 6 neutrons and carbon-14 has 8.
Some isotopes are radioactive. Their nuclei are unstable and break down over time, giving off radiation. Many isotopes are not radioactive.

Relative atomic mass is a weighted average of the masses of an element's isotopes. Isotopes that are more abundant count for more. If an element is mostly one isotope, its relative atomic mass is close to that isotope's mass number.
draft.remember: Same protons, different neutrons. Relative atomic mass is an average that favours the more abundant isotopes.

a.q: Atom X has 17 protons and 18 neutrons. Atom Y has 17 protons and 20 neutrons. How are X and Y related?
opts: They are isotopes of the same element
They are atoms of different elements
They are ions of the same element
They are atoms of the same element with equal mass numbers
a.why: Both atoms have 17 protons, so they are the same element. They differ in neutrons, so they are isotopes. The mass numbers are 35 and 37, so they are not equal.
a.clue: Compare the protons first, then the neutrons.

b.q: Element Z has two isotopes: 90% has a mass number of 20 and 10% has a mass number of 22. Which value is closest to its relative atomic mass?
b.why: The average is weighted: (0.90 × 20) + (0.10 × 22) = 20.2. The simple average of 20 and 22 is 21.0, which is tempting, but it ignores that the lighter isotope is far more abundant.
b.clue: The more abundant isotope counts for more in the average.

a.best: They are isotopes of the same element

problems.detail: The carbon-12 and carbon-14 neutron example sits in the bullet about isotopes reacting the same way, after the reason about electrons. A student may read it as illustrating reactivity rather than different neutron numbers. It belongs with the first bullet.

check.summary: Both questions are correct with one clear answer each, and the explanations match. One minor issue: the carbon isotope example is placed in the bullet about chemical reactivity instead of the bullet defining isotopes.
